terms.comment: Classically a territory outside Italy under a Roman governor, Sicily the first of them (Cic. Verr. 2.2.2); also any charge given to a magistrate, and in comedy any job one takes on (Plaut., Ter.). A modern province is a division of a country; Levi and Bini (p. 52) say to give prōvincia that new sense, or to use regiō.

phrases.latin: prīma omnium, id quod ōrnāmentum imperī est, prōvincia est appellāta
phrases.english: (Sicily) was the first of all to be called a province, the jewel of our empire

phrases.latin: Baetica … cūnctās prōvinciārum dīvitī cultū et quōdam fertilī ac peculiārī nitōre praecēdit
phrases.english: Baetica outdoes all the provinces in the richness of its farming and a fertile brilliance of its own

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. political division: province (Canada).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 180.
